questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam because it offered many english taight courses courses that fit well with my studies at UCPH. I also wished to spend the semester in a major European city, and Amsterdam seemed like a great choice because of its unique charm, international environment, and vibrant student life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall, it was quite easy. The university sent all information by email before the semester started, and most practical information was available online. There were a few things I had to look up myself, but I generally found the information I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome programme for exchange students, which was helpful for getting practical information and meeting other students. The Incoming Exchange team was also easy to contact if I had any questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through DUWO, which have several housing opportunities across the city. I lived at Campus Uilenstede, which I can definitely recommend, as most exchange students live there, which made it easy to meet new people, and there was a great sense of community.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus was a great experience and gave me more independence. If possible, I would recommend living somewhere with other exchange students, as it makes it much easier to meet people and build a social network from the beginning. It is also worth knowing that cycling is the easiest way to get around Amsterdam, so commuting to campus is usually quick and convenient.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was straightforward. I received clear instructions before the semester started, and all the registration was done online. However, there were several deadlines to keep track of. First, the courses had to be pre-approved by the host university, and only afterwards could I register for them. As long as I paid attention to the deadlines, it went smoothly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Incoming Exchange team was available if I had questions about registration or practical matters, and they answered quickly to my emails. There was also information online, and teachers were approachable if I had questions about the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There were a couple of classes which I found out late that I unfortunately could not sign up for, since these were only available for psychology students, and this information was not available on the University's website. But besides this, I got registered for all the classes that I wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to read the emails from the university carefully and be aware of the deadlines. If something is unclear, contact the Incoming Exchange team - they were helpful and replied quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took both Bachelor's and Master's level courses during my exchange. Overall, I found the academic level to be comparable to UCPH. The Master's courses were slightly more challenging, but for me, the level of difficulty mainly depended on how closely the course matched my own field of study. Courses outside my main area of study required more time and preparation than those that were more closely related to my academic background.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was quite similar to UCPH. There was a combination of lectures and smaller classes with discussions and group work. Students were expected to prepare before class and participate actively, so I found it easy to adapt. However, we had many more group projects, presentations and assignments than we are used to at my studies at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Beyond Gender Inequalities, Ethics of Public Health, Science Communication for Researchers, AI & Society, EU Anti-Discrimination Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all the courses I took, as I think they were all interesting and educational. However, depending on your study programme, some are more relevant than others.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The biggest unexpected costs were personal expenses, such as social activities, going out, and drinks. These costs added up more than I had expected, as it was an opportunity to socialize with other exchange students. Other than that, the overall cost of living was quite similar to what I was used to in Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and eating out were generally the same or slightly less expensive than in Denmark. Public transport were more expensive than what I expected, but since I mainly cycled around the city, I did not spend that much on transportation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university offered sports, student associations, cultural events, and activities organised by ESN and other student organisations. There were also introduction events, social gatherings, and day trips for exchange students. Since I lived at Campus Uilenstede, where many exchange students lived, it was also very easy to meet people and take part in social activities outside of the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining the introduction activities at the beginning of the semester and participating in events organised for exchange students, especially those of ESN, as they are a great way to meet new people quickly. I met most of my friends through these events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend exploring Amsterdam by bike and visiting different neighbourhoods, museums, and parks. It is also easy to take day trips to other Dutch cities such as Utrecht, Rotterdam, or The Hague. Since Amsterdam has good international transport connections, it is also a great opportunity to visit nearby countries during longer weekends. I e.g. went to Antwerp and Paris by train/bus, both which I can recommend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it easy to adjust. Most people spoke excellent English, and the city is very international, which made settling in quite straightforward. I also think the local culture in Amsterdam is pretty similar to in Copenhagen/Denmark, so I didn't really experience any culture shock.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found it more difficult to socialize with Dutch than international students, as international students are definitely more open to meeting new people. But participating actively in classes and group work made it easier to get to know both Dutch and international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any major cultural differences that were difficult to adapt to. Dutch people are generally quite direct in their communication, which can take some getting used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the cycling culture and how easy it was to get around the city by bike. I also liked the relaxed and open atmosphere, as well as how international Amsterdam is, which made it easy to feel welcome.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Start looking for accommodation as early as possible, as finding housing in Amsterdam can be challenging.
2. Take part in introduction activities and social events at the beginning of the semester, as this is the easiest way to meet new people and build a social network.
3. Be open to new experiences and say yes to opportunities, even if they are outside your comfort zone. The exchange goes by quickly, so make the most of it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend living somewhere with other exchange students if possible, as it makes it much easier to meet people and create a social life. Campus Uilenstede was a great place to live for this reason. I would also recommend getting a bike (e.g. through Swapfiets), as cycling is the easiest way to get around Amsterdam and is a big part of everyday life.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange was meeting people from many different countries and cultures. I made friendships that I would not have made otherwise, and I really enjoyed the spontaneity of everyday life during the exchange. The experience also helped me become more independent and confident in new situations.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was probably adapting to a new environment and building a new social network from scratch. In the beginning, everything was unfamiliar, but after the first few weeks it became much easier. Another challenge was balancing studies, social activities, and exploring a new city, as there were many things to experience during the semester.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
